content.value: Read the structure of a Java class; distinguish instance fields, constructors, methods, and local variables; choose access modifiers.

A class body can contain fields, constructors, and methods. Instance fields describe each object’s state and are declared outside method bodies. Constructors initialize new objects. Methods provide behavior, with parameters and local variables that exist only during their invocation or block. These roles differ even when names look similar.

Declare representation fields private and expose deliberate public operations. Numeric fields receive default zero values, boolean fields default to false, and reference fields default to null before constructor initialization. Local variables do not follow that rule: they must be definitely assigned before use. A reusable class need not have its own main method.

count is the stored per-object field. start is a constructor parameter copied into that field. getCount returns the current state, while increment changes it. Two separately constructed Counters have independent count fields.

Do not declare a supposed persistent field inside a constructor; that would create a local variable instead. private does not mean constant, and public does not mean static. Use final only when reassignment must be prohibited.
Add a public reset method that assigns count = 0 and returns no value. Then trace a Counter constructed with 3, incremented twice, and reset: its values are 3, 4, 5, and 0.
